sections.heading: About this notice
paragraphs: GradeBook is a learning platform. This installation of GradeBook is run by {{controller}} for its schools: staff use it to run courses, set and mark work, take attendance and keep pastoral records, students use it to see their work and grades, and parents and guardians use it to follow their child's progress.

This notice explains what personal data this GradeBook processes, why, on what lawful basis, who receives it, how long it is kept and what rights you have. It covers students, parents and guardians, staff and anyone else whose information is in it, and is written to meet Articles 12 to 14 of the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Where local law gives you more protection, that law applies.

The details of the organisation, the services it uses and how long data is kept are filled in from this installation's live settings, so they show what this GradeBook actually does. The people who make the GradeBook software do not receive any data from this installation.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data
paragraphs: {{controller}} decides how and why this GradeBook processes personal data, so it is the controller. Where a school in the organisation is a separate legal body, that school is also a controller for its own records; your school can tell you which applies.

sections.heading: What data we process
paragraphs: Depending on your role and the features your school uses, this GradeBook processes:

list.text: your name, email address, optional profile picture and account type. If you sign in with Google, Microsoft or your school's own sign-in, we also receive an identifier for that account and the name and email address it shares.
name, student number, gender, date of birth, enrolment dates, year group, the courses a student takes, and links to parents or guardians with their contact details.

extra time, a quiz exemption from Lockdown and similar adjustments, with the reason. A reason can reveal health or disability information, which is special category data. Only staff with permission to see sensitive details can read it, and it is stored encrypted.
course content, assignments, quiz answers, submitted files and text, marks, rubric assessments, feedback, grades, report comments, report cards, discussion posts and announcements.
check-in times, how the student checked in, attendance status, and absence alerts. If a teacher turns on the location check, see "Location check-ins" below.

notes staff write about behaviour, wellbeing and safeguarding concerns, with follow-ups and attachments. They can contain special category data (for example about health) and are stored encrypted. Safeguarding notes are visible only to staff the school has given that permission.
chat messages (encrypted in the database) and the files you upload or share.

for a quiz the teacher set to Lockdown, whether the student is away from the quiz screen, how many times they left it, when they last left it and how (for example, switching tab or leaving full screen). Students with a Lockdown exemption are not monitored.

for each signed-in session: a device label (such as "Chrome on macOS"), the IP address, browser or app details, and when it was created and last used, which you can see and end under Signed-in devices. Also one-time sign-in codes, the devices you have signed in on (without IP addresses) for new sign-in alerts, an authenticator app secret if you set one up (encrypted) with its recovery codes (stored only in a form that cannot be read back), and, in the mobile app, a push notification token.

who changed which school record and when, who read safeguarding notes, single sign-on and integration changes, and a log of AI requests (who, when, which feature; not the text, unless the organisation turned on keeping prompts for troubleshooting).

sections.heading: Where the data comes from
paragraphs: Most data is entered by you or by your school: staff create student records, mark work and write notes; students hand in work; parents accept an invitation to link to their child. Some data comes from elsewhere:

list.text: if the school uses rostering, student, staff, class and enrolment records are copied in from it (a OneRoster connection or a CSV file).
Google, Microsoft or your school's own identity provider confirm who you are and share your name and email address.
a learning tool the school connected (LTI) can send back a grade for work done in it.

sections.heading: Why we use it and on what lawful basis
paragraphs: We use personal data only to run the school's teaching, assessment, communication and safeguarding, and to keep GradeBook secure. The table shows each purpose and the lawful basis {{controller}} relies on. Special category data (health or similar information in accommodations and pastoral notes) is processed only under an Article 9 condition, shown next to those purposes.
sections.footer: We do not sell personal data, use it for advertising, or build marketing profiles. Data is not used to train artificial intelligence models.

sections.heading: How each feature uses data
paragraphs: Some features are switched on or off by the organisation or the school; the ones currently in use are marked.

list.text: staff can ask the AI provider listed below to draft course plans, questions and feedback suggestions. Before anything is sent, the student's and classmates' names, email addresses and phone numbers are replaced with placeholders. A student's work is sent for feedback suggestions only if the school has allowed it, and never for a student whose school has switched AI off for them. A teacher reviews every suggestion; nothing is published or graded automatically.

nothing is translated until you choose a language, and only on the website. Then the interface text and course content on the page you are viewing are sent to the translation service listed below. Pages about individual people (messages, pastoral notes, a student's record, analytics and at-risk lists, audit logs) are never sent, and names, grades, marks, feedback and email addresses shown on other pages are marked so they are left out. What you type into forms is never sent. Personal details written inside course content itself (for example a pupil's name in an announcement) are sent with that content. Google's and Yandex's translation services offer no data processing agreement, so GradeBook refuses them unless the server operator has explicitly allowed them. Translations are cached on the server for a short time (see retention) and in your browser tab until you sign out. Choosing English again stops it.

a school can send chosen events (for example a grade or attendance change) to its own systems. Accommodation reasons and pastoral notes are never sent. A new webhook address must use an encrypted (https) connection, unless the server operator allows plain http for the organisation's own private network; a webhook saved with http before that rule keeps working until its address is changed, and the school's settings mark it as unencrypted. A school administrator can turn off certificate checking for a webhook (for example, for an internal server with its own certificate); that change is recorded and the school's and organisation's administrators are emailed.
when you open a tool the school connected, it receives a pseudonymous id, your role and the course, and your name or email address only if the organisation allowed that tool to receive them.
the school's management information system sends GradeBook its students, staff, classes and enrolments, so records stay in step. GradeBook does not send student data back to it.
parents and guardians the school links to a student can see that student's courses, grades, attendance, reports and announcements, and receive email notices the parent can switch off.
when a student's absences meet a rule the school set, the staff responsible (and parents, if the school chose) are notified. The alert is a prompt; a person decides what to do.

staff see course summaries and lists that name the students who meet the school's rule-based criteria (for example missing work or low attendance), with the reasons. These are prompts for staff to look more closely, not automated decisions about you. A school can leave a student out of at-risk lists; they still count in course totals and averages.
submitted text is compared with other submissions in the school to point out possible copying. A teacher reviews any match; the score alone decides nothing. A school can switch it off for a student.

staff record concerns so the school can support and protect students. Notes are encrypted, each time staff open or list notes is logged, and safeguarding notes are limited to designated staff. Notes are included when the school answers a subject access request, but a note may be withheld, with a recorded reason, where the law allows it (for example, to protect a child).

the quiz notices when a student leaves the quiz screen and shows the teacher when and how they left (for example, switching tab or leaving full screen) and how many times; it does not record the screen, camera or microphone.

the mobile app receives notifications through Expo and Apple's or Google's push services, which see the device token and the notification text. Unless the school or the organisation chooses otherwise, notifications about a child (grades, attendance, parent notices, discussion replies) say only "You have a new update", and course news (new work, announcements) shows its title and text. A school, or the organisation for all schools, can make every notification generic or every notification full. You can switch kinds of notification off in your settings.

only when a teacher turns on the location check: your device's location is read at the moment you check in and used to work out your distance from the check-in point. GradeBook keeps that distance, how accurate your device said the reading was, and markers for readings that look copied or typed in, which staff can see; the markers alone never stop a check-in. The coordinates themselves are cleared when the session closes, and any left over are removed within {{locationRetention}} after it closes. Your device asks your permission first. While a session is open, a teacher can also share their own device's location so the check-in point follows the class; only course staff see that point, and it is cleared in the same way.

sections.heading: Automated decisions
paragraphs: GradeBook does not make decisions about you that are based solely on automated processing and have legal or similarly significant effects (Article 22). Quiz questions with fixed answers are marked automatically, and teachers can review and change those marks. At-risk lists, attendance alerts, similarity scores and AI suggestions are prompts for staff, and a person decides what happens next.

sections.heading: Who receives your data
paragraphs: Inside a school, staff, students and parents see only what their role allows. Outside it, data goes only to the service providers (processors) below, which process it for {{controller}} under written agreements, and to providers a school or you chose (sign-in providers, external tools, webhooks). This list is generated from this installation's current configuration.
sections.footer: Data may also be disclosed when the law requires it, for example to a court, the police or a child protection agency, or to protect someone's life.

sections.heading: International transfers
paragraphs: If a provider above processes data outside the UK or the European Economic Area in a country without an adequacy decision, {{controller}} uses the safeguards the GDPR requires, such as the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses or the UK International Data Transfer Agreement. You can ask {{contact}} for a copy.

paragraphs: Data is kept only as long as it is needed. These periods are this installation's settings:

sections.heading: How data is protected
paragraphs: Connections to GradeBook are encrypted (HTTPS). Every request is checked on the server against the person's role and permissions. Chat messages, pastoral notes, accommodation reasons, stored secrets and authenticator app secrets are encrypted in the database, backups are encrypted before they leave the server, and staff can protect their account with an authenticator app, which the organisation can require for administrators and safeguarding staff. Changes to school records and reads of safeguarding notes are recorded in an audit log that cannot be edited.

{{controller}} is responsible for the servers this runs on. If a personal data breach happens, it will tell the supervisory authority within 72 hours where the law requires, and tell you without undue delay if the breach is likely to put you at high risk.

sections.heading: Your rights and how to use them
paragraphs: You have these rights. Many of them you can use yourself, in the app:

list.bold: Access and a copy of your data
list.text: download a copy of your data from your settings (staff in account settings, students in the student portal). Parents can download what the school shows them about their child from the parent portal. The school can produce a fuller copy for a student, including the messages the student sent, their files, sign-in sessions and devices, and records staff keep about them. A download is kept for a short time and then deleted.
the download is a machine-readable file (JSON plus your files) that you can take to another service.

change your name and profile picture in your account settings. To change your email address, enter the new one and confirm it with a code sent to it. Ask your school to correct school records such as grades or attendance.

delete your account from your account settings; if your school manages your account through its own sign-in, ask the school. School records about you (such as grades and attendance) are kept or erased by the school under its own retention rules; ask the school if you think they should be erased. The school can erase a student record, and the organisation can delete a user account.

ask your school to restrict or stop processing. For an individual student it can stop their work being sent to AI assistance, leave their work out of similarity checks, and leave them out of at-risk lists. You can switch kinds of email and push notification off in your settings, and parents can do the same for notices about their child in the parent portal.
where processing is based on consent (translation), choose English again at any time. This does not affect what happened before.

list.bold: Not be subject to automated decisions
list.text: see "Automated decisions" above.

sections.footer: For anything you cannot do in the app, contact {{contact}}. We reply within one month (longer only for complex requests, and we will tell you why). Requests about school records are handled together with your school.

sections.heading: Complaints
paragraphs: If you are unhappy with how your data is handled, please tell {{contact}} first so it can be put right. You also have the right to complain to a data protection supervisory authority, in particular in the country where you live or work or where the problem happened.

sections.heading: Cookies and storage on your device
paragraphs: GradeBook stores only what it needs to work or to remember a choice you made. There are no advertising, analytics or tracking cookies, and nothing is shared with third parties for those purposes, so there is no cookie banner.

sections.heading: If you are a student
paragraphs: This part is for you, in plain words.

Your school uses GradeBook to give you your work, mark it, take attendance and keep you safe. Your teachers can see your work, your grades and your attendance. Your parents or guardians can see them too if the school has linked them to you. Some staff can write notes about how you are doing and if they are worried about you, so they can help.
list: We do not sell your information or use it for adverts.
A computer never makes big decisions about you on its own. A teacher always checks.
If your teacher turns on the location check for attendance, your phone shares where you are only at the moment you check in. We keep how far away you were, not where you were.
You can download a copy of your information from your settings in the student portal.
If something about you is wrong, tell your teacher or the school office and they will fix it.
If you are worried about how your information is used, talk to a teacher or a parent, or contact {{contact}}. You can also complain to the data protection authority shown above.

sections.heading: Changes to this notice
paragraphs: This notice changes when the software or this installation's settings change. The date at the top shows when the text was last revised; the lists filled in from the live settings are always current. If a change affects how your data is used, {{controller}} will tell you.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: For questions about this notice or to use your rights, contact {{contact}}.

cookies.name: gb_session
cookies.purpose: Keeps you signed in. Secure and not readable by page scripts.
cookies.duration: Until you sign out or the session ends (see "Signed-in sessions" in the retention table)

cookies.name: gb_sso_flow
cookies.purpose: Protects a single sign-on attempt against tampering while you are at the sign-in provider.

cookies.name: gb_scan_device
cookies.purpose: A random id for the browser that scanned an attendance QR code, so the check-in cannot be forwarded to another phone.

cookies.name: sidebar_state
cookies.purpose: Remembers whether you collapsed the side menu.

cookies.name: gb_language
cookies.purpose: Remembers the language you chose, including "no thanks", so you are asked only once.

cookies.name: gb_translation_cache:*
cookies.purpose: Translations of the pages you viewed, so they are not requested again.
cookies.duration: Until you close the tab or sign out
cookies.kind: Strictly necessary for translation you asked for

cookies.name: gb_mfa_challenge
cookies.purpose: Holds a sign-in in progress while you enter the code from your authenticator app, so it is not put in the page address.
cookies.duration: Removed as soon as the code step reads it, or when the tab is closed

cookies.name: attendance-claim:*
cookies.purpose: Carries an attendance QR check-in across sign-in.
cookies.duration: Until the check-in is done or the tab is closed

cookies.name: gb_session_token
cookies.purpose: Keeps you signed in to the app.
cookies.duration: Until you sign out or the session ends

cookies.name: gb_server_url
cookies.purpose: The school server the app connects to.

cookies.name: gb_sso_pending
cookies.purpose: A single sign-on attempt in progress.

cookies.name: gb_update_dismissed
cookies.purpose: Remembers that you dismissed an app update notice.

cookies.name: Offline copies and drafts
cookies.purpose: Unsent quiz answers and saved copies of your work so the app works offline.
cookies.duration: Removed when you sign out or change server
